messages:
Priya (Support): FYI -- customer Luis reporting a spike of 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. Getting lots of 504s and high p99 latency. He says it started after a traffic bump.
Luis (Customer): Repro: POST /v1/generate with streaming=false, ~350 concurrent short requests (avg 120 tokens). Errors: a mix of 504 Gateway Timeout and a few 502s. Example error body: `{\"error\":\"upstream request timed out\"}`.
Luis (Customer): We never changed our client. Started around 09:05, then got worse. Token bill spike too. Need ETA.
Priya (Support): Adding SRE / eng. @Dana can you triage queue/backpressure? Customer org: org_89tx.
infra-bot: Alert: hosted-gateway queue_depth per-node crossed threshold (5000) at 2026-03-14T09:07:12Z for tenant org_89tx :metric.queue_depth=5124 :severity=warning
Dana (SRE): I'm looking at gateway metrics. Seeing sustained queue depth high across the X/Y batcher ring for org_89tx. Continuous batching backlog forms when many small requests block a batch waiting for long-running requests to finish. p95->p99 latency jumped first, then we hit early_rejects.
Dana (SRE): Correlating with model variant rtx-3-small-quant; those instances have lower throughput and a KV-cache retention bug (investigating) which makes some requests hold a slot for extra ~700-900ms. That amplifies batcher tail.
Mason (Eng): Can you confirm whether queue_depth limit was reached or we saw head-of-line blocking?
Dana (SRE): Both. Queue depth reached configured soft limit 5000 and we fell back to early_reject policy => some requests got 429/early-reject, others timed out at the gateway 504s because kv-cache hold caused batch not to flush.
Mason (Eng): Ok. Short-term mitigation: per-tenant route throttle + increase queue_depth for org_89tx to 12000, and enable per-route small-request prioritization to favor short requests. I'll prepare the change.
Priya (Support): Luis, we'll increase your limit and apply throttle to shed the noisy clients. Expect a follow-up in ~10-15m.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/patch/batcher-prioritization v2 -> batcher-service (canary 10%)
Dana (SRE): Also rolling restart of batcher pods on the affected AZ to flush stuck KV caches: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher-service -n hosted-inference --field-selector=metadata.labels.az=us-west-2a`. Doing one AZ at a time.
Mason (Eng): Config to patch via admin API: 
```
POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routes/org_89tx/config
{
  "queue_depth": 12000,
  "early_reject_threshold": 0.9,
  "prioritize_short_requests": true
}
```
Applying now.
Dana (SRE): After first AZ restart and config change I see queue depth drop from ~5100->900 within 60s and 504s drop to baseline. p99 latency for org_89tx reduced from 3.2s -> 0.85s.
Luis (Customer): Seeing much better now, thanks. Any root cause guidance? Will this happen again?
Mason (Eng): Root cause: combination of (1) traffic shape: many concurrent short requests mixed with a smaller fraction of long requests, (2) an inefficient hold in the KV cache path on this model variant that increased per-request hold time, and (3) queue_depth soft limits that delayed early shedding until saturation. The continuous batching runtime prefers to wait to fill batches which causes head-of-line long requests to delay small ones.
Dana (SRE): Permanent fix plan: a) patch KV cache retention bug (PR #4521) to avoid the 700-900ms hold, b) add dynamic request prioritization (PR #4538) so small requests get dispatched earlier, c) make per-tenant adaptive queue_depth that scales with observed tail latency.
Mason (Eng): PRs linked and code review in progress. We'll backport the KV fix to the 2026-02 runtime branch.
Priya (Support): I've opened ticket RDW-3247 and assigned to Mason/Dana. Luis I'll email the postmortem once we have it.
Dana (SRE): Follow-ups: monitor org_89tx:queue_depth, batcher_hold_ms, kv_cache_retention_ms for 24h. Set alert to 4000 instead of 5000 for this tenant as a precaution.
Mason (Eng): Note for runbook: repro steps to simulate the backlog:
1) run 350 concurrent clients with short requests (100-140 tokens) + 5 long requests (3-4k tokens) pinned to same model variant.
2) use this load script (wrk-like):
```
for i in 1..350 do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
    -d '{"model":"rtx-3-small-quant","input":"short prompt"}' &
done
# then after 3s start 5 long requests
```
This reproduces the head-of-line blocking in our lab.
Priya (Support): Customer happy for now; keeping ticket open pending the PRs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Mason (Eng): I'll post PR links here when merged. Dana, ping me if anything regresses.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: batcher-prioritization v2 -> batcher-service (100%)
Dana (SRE): Closing incident once metrics stable for 2h. Leaving ticket RDW-3247 open for the follow-up work.
Priya (Support): Marking as customer-resolved and following up with postmortem later.
